newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena to invest in Congo's Grands Hotels.
newsitem.headline: Sabena to invest in Congo's Grands Hotels.

text.p: Belgian airline Sabena SA confirmed on Friday it planned to invest 650 million Belgian francs in bourse-listed hotel unit Cie des Grands Hotels Africains as part of a capital increase.
Grands Hotels' main asset is a hotel in Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo (formerly Zaire).
In a statement in Belgian newspapers Grands Hotels said Sabena would in return receive 17,500,000 new shares, legally identical to the company's existing 1,125,000 shares.
The capital increase is due to be voted on at a meeting of Grands Hotels shareholders meeting in Kinshasa on July 7.
Sabena at present owns 79.81 percent of Grands Hotels. A spokesman said it was too early to say what percentage of shares it would hold following the capital increase.
"It will depend on whether the other shareholders follow (the capital increase)," he told Reuters.
He added the operation was needed to recapitalise the company, which had invested heavily in its hotel between 1989 and 1994, drawing on its own funds.
Sabena is 49.5 percent owned by Switzerland's Swissair group. Apart from the hotel in Congo, Sabena controls hotel units in Rwanda and Guinea. It also owns two hotels in Belgium.
